# wugweb-seo

**Version 2.5.0** · Wugweb · November 2026

Plan, audit and report on how Wugweb pages are found in search engines and AI answers. Plan gives the site keyword and intent map, the phrase, intent, outline and brief limits for one page, and keyword notes for social and portfolio titles. Audit checks the rendered page and robots.txt and returns a fix list split three ways. Report reads Search Console and AI answer data and feeds the content plan. It never writes copy and changes nothing itself. Every helper is optional; the rules taken from them are restated in the references. Two check scripts with no dependencies. Independent of CMS, host and agent.

A page is found in two ways: a search engine ranks it, or an AI answer quotes
it. Both read the same things: what the page claims, how its server HTML is
built, and what its structured data says.

This skill has three parts, used in this order:

1. **Plan.** Before a page is written, give the target phrase, the intent and
   the limits the writer must meet.
2. **Audit.** After a page is built, check it and return a fix list.
3. **Report.** After a page is live, read the data and say what to improve next.

It returns constraints, checks and reports. It never writes or rewrites page
copy, and it changes no file, page or record itself.

This file works alone. The `references/` files hold the full checklists and
templates for each part.

If a sibling is not installed, give this skill's answer, say which sibling

## Apply the fixed rules

The owner set these. They win over anything a helper skill suggests.

### On every site

These apply to wugweb.com, client sites, Kits and Wugweb X.

- **Never propose** `HowTo`, review stars, `llms.txt` or a keyword density
  target.
- **FAQPage only where the page shows the questions.** Use `FAQPage` only for
  questions and answers the page visibly carries, from its `faqs` field,
  written by `wugweb-work`. Every question and answer in the markup appears on
  the page. Never ask for an FAQ block to win search. Google ended FAQ rich
  results on 7 May 2026, so the markup earns no Google feature.
- **Headings belong to the copy.** Wugweb headings are claims. Check them for
  length and order; never ask for a question heading or a rewrite.
- **Dates.** Where a page shows a date, it matches the schema date.
- **Rendered title** 60 characters or fewer. Other title and description
  limits for these sites are not decided. Every character limit in this skill
  is a house limit: Google sets none and cuts titles to the device width.

### On wugweb.com only

- **One address per page.** One slug per case study. Add no redirects for old
  or Framer addresses.
- **Title.** For a case study, the source title is 51 characters or fewer. The
  site adds " | Wugweb" only when the title does not already name Wugweb and
  the total fits in 60. The limit for other page types is not decided. The
  audit does not check titles for dashes.
- **Description.** 140 to 160 characters.
- **Schema on the main site address only.** A case study carries `WebPage`,
  `CreativeWork` and `BreadcrumbList`. Wugweb is `creator` and `publisher`.
  There is no `author`. A blog post carries `BlogPosting` with a `Person`
  author. The layout already emits `Organization`, `WebSite` and the founder on
  every page; leave them. Schema for service pages, home and about is not
  decided.
- **Dates shown.** A blog post shows its date. A case study shows none.
- **AI files.** Leave `public/llms.txt` and `ai-context.txt` as they are;
  never recommend them.
- **The source.** Notion holds the SEO fields of a case study and every blog
  post. Propose a change to a field as current → proposed. The owner approves
  it and the maker skill writes it.

## Use the plan part before a page is written

Two callers use this part. `wugweb-strategy` asks for the site keyword and
intent map, topic gaps and pages to refresh. `wugweb-work` asks for one page,
as below, or for a keyword note for a LinkedIn, Behance or Dribbble title and
tags. Never write the post; no hashtag stuffing.

For one page, answer one question: which phrase and intent should it target?

1. Read what the maker sends: the page, its audience, what was built, and
   candidate phrases in the owner's words.
2. Group the candidates by the intent the live results show: someone learning,
   comparing, hiring or looking for Wugweb by name.
3. Look at the results that rank now. Note their format and the entities they
   name.
4. Choose one primary phrase and up to three supporting phrases. Give each its
   source: Search Console, a keyword tool with the date, or "unvalidated".
5. Return the brief constraints in the shape in `references/plan.md`.

Return limits and an outline, never wording: the title limit, the description
limit, the entities the page must name, the schema, the link rules, and an
outline. `wugweb-strategy` decides which pages a piece links to. This skill
owns the link rules: one link up to the service pillar and two or three across
to sibling pages, descriptive anchors, no orphans or dead ends, and depth from
home. It audits the result.
The outline lists the topics the page must cover, in order, with the fact from
the source each one rests on. It names topics, not headings; the maker writes
the headings. Do not add an FAQ
block, keyword counts or sections written for search.

When two pages would target the same phrase, say so and name both. The owner
decides which keeps it.

## Use the audit part after a page is built

Check the rendered page, not the source document. Use a local preview served
with the canonical host, or the live address.

### 1. Run the page check

```bash
node scripts/check-page.mjs page.html --kind work --host wugweb.com
```

It reads the HTML and reports title, description, H1, canonical, robots meta,
share tags, images, server HTML text and JSON-LD. Each finding carries a severity and a
check id. Read its "Not checked" lines and repeat them.

### 2. Run the crawler check

```bash
node scripts/check-robots.mjs robots.txt --path /work/slug
```

It resolves, for each named bot, whether the path is allowed. Search and
citation bots must reach every page that should be found. Whether to allow
training bots is the owner's choice; report what the file says and ask once
per property.

### 3. Check what the scripts cannot see

Work through the manual list in `references/audit.md`:

- a firewall or bot setting that returns 403 to crawlers while robots.txt
  allows them;
- redirect chains, and the http, https, www and bare host forms;
- the sitemap: present, listed in robots.txt, canonical 200 addresses only;
- Core Web Vitals from field data: LCP 2.5 seconds or less, INP 200
  milliseconds or less, CLS 0.1 or less;
- that the schema matches what the page shows.

### 4. Score the page: citability and keyphrase

Two scores, both in `references/audit.md`. The citability score (0 to 100) is
the AI-answer score: score each section on the five criteria, weight by length,
report the page score and the three weakest sections. The keyphrase score (0 to
100) is the search score, modelled on Rank Math:

```bash
node scripts/score-page.mjs page.html --keyword "<phrase>" --host wugweb.com
```

Both scores report; neither rewrites. Name what is weak; the maker acts.

### 5. Return the fix list

Split it three ways. A finding on one page goes to `wugweb-work` as current
→ proposed. A finding that repeats on every page using a block (alt text,
lazy loading, heading order, image sizes) goes to `wugweb-kits`, which answers
with its check result. A code fix goes in the developer block below.

## Use the report part after a page is live

The report feeds `wugweb-strategy`'s planning. Reporting on posts belongs
there, not here.

1. Name the source and the date range of every number. A Search Console
   export is the standard source; a connected SEO data tool is optional. If
   neither is given, ask for the export and stop.
2. Compare the period with the one before and with the same period a year
   earlier.
3. List the pages that rose and fell most.
4. Flag two quick wins:
   - queries with many impressions and a low click rate, which point to the
     title and description;
   - pages at positions 8 to 20, which point to the content.
5. Report AI answer presence from a fixed monthly prompt sample: cited,
   mentioned or absent per prompt. Read the trend over months.

For a drop, check in this order: tracking, then indexing, robots.txt or a
deploy, then the date of a search engine update, then a results feature taking
the click, then a competitor, then content decay.

Search Console data is sampled. Read it as a trend. Never place these numbers
on a case study as a client result. The shape is in `references/report.md`.

## Report findings in this shape

Give computed totals first, then one line per finding sorted by severity. Each
line carries the severity, the place, the finding and the check id.

```
1 page. 2 blockers, 1 high, 1 medium.

BLOCKER  <title>          source title 58 characters, limit 51     title-length
BLOCKER  JSON-LD          HowTo present                            schema-banned-type
HIGH     <img> 3 of 7     no width and height                      img-dimensions
MEDIUM   body             112 words in server HTML                 server-html-text
```

State what was not checked. If the page passes, say it passes and stop. Never
invent a finding.

## Hand code fixes to a developer

End an audit that needs code with this block:

```
SEO fixes: <site>, <date>
Scope: <routes or files>
1. BLOCKER <what to change>. Check: <how to confirm it>
2. ...
Copy, layout and tokens are out of scope.
```

## Work from real data only

Every phrase volume, ranking and traffic number comes from a named tool and
date. If a number could not be fetched, say so and mark the phrase
"unvalidated". A stated gap is a complete answer.

Third-party figures about AI answers, such as the share of citations taken
from the top of a page, are directional. Give the source and date, or leave
them out. When community advice contradicts the search engine's own guidance,
follow the search engine and say so.

The helper skills that back each part are in `references/handoffs.md`. Every
helper is optional: the rules this skill took from them are restated in the
"Absorbed rules" sections of `references/plan.md`, `references/audit.md` and
`references/report.md`, so each part can be done by hand. A
helper returns a proposal or a report; only a Wugweb skill writes anything,
and only after the owner approves.

## Fit the size of the request

When the user asks for one check, do that check. Then name, in one sentence,
the next check that would help most. Do not run all three parts for someone who
asked about one title.

## Leave these decisions to the owner

- Which page keeps a phrase two pages want.
- Whether training bots may crawl.
- The title limit for blog posts and service pages.
- Schema for service pages, home and about.
- Title and description limits for client sites, Kits and Wugweb X.

## Run the scripts

Five scripts, all Node 18 or later, no packages: `check-page.mjs`,
`score-page.mjs`, `check-robots.mjs`, `validate.mjs`, `test.mjs` and the
generator `build.mjs`. The exact commands, flags and fixtures are in
`README.md`.

## Use outside Claude

The folder is a standard Agent Skill, so any agent that reads `SKILL.md` loads
it as it is. `AGENTS.md` is the whole skill compiled into one file for agents
that read plain instructions. `adapters/` holds a Cursor rule and an
instruction block for a custom GPT. `scripts/build.mjs` generates all of
these; edit the sources, never the output. Install steps for each agent are in
`README.md`.

Decline and record any helper answer that asks for:

- `HowTo`, review stars or aggregate ratings, or `FAQPage` for questions the page does not show;

## Plan: brief constraints before a page is written

The plan part answers one question for a maker skill: which phrase and intent
should this page target, and what limits must the copy meet? It returns limits
and an outline of topics, never wording.

### What the maker sends

```
Page: <path> | Type: <case study, blog post, service page> | Client: <name or none>
What was built or said (one sentence):
Audience: <who would read this and why>
Candidate phrases (owner's words only):
Question: which one phrase and intent should this page target?
```

If a field is missing, ask for it once. Do not guess the audience.

### Classify intent from the live results

| Intent | The searcher wants to | Results that usually rank |
|---|---|---|
| Learning | understand a subject | guides, explainers |
| Comparing | weigh options | lists, comparisons, case studies |
| Hiring | find someone to do the work | service pages, case studies, agency pages |
| By name | reach Wugweb itself | the home page, about page |

Read the intent from the results that rank now, not from the words alone. Match
the format those results share.

### Choose the phrases

1. Group the candidates by intent.
2. Drop any phrase whose results serve a different intent from the page.
3. Choose one primary phrase and up to three supporting phrases.
4. Give each phrase its source: Search Console with the date range, a keyword
   tool with the date, or "unvalidated".
5. Rank by fit with the page and with the work Wugweb wants, then by how
   winnable the current results look. Volume breaks ties only.

If another page already targets the primary phrase, name both pages and stop.
The owner decides which keeps it.

### Return this shape

```
Page: <path>
Intent: <learning, comparing, hiring or by name>, from <how it was read>
Primary phrase: <phrase> (<source and date, or unvalidated>)
Supporting phrases: <phrase> (<source>), ...
Format that ranks now: <format>, seen on <up to three addresses>
Entities the page must name: <people, products, places, numbers already in the source>
Title: source 51 characters or fewer for a case study; other types not decided
Description: 140 to 160 characters
Schema: <types, from the fixed rules>
Links: targets from wugweb-strategy; rules: one up to the pillar, two or three
  across to siblings, descriptive anchors, no orphans or dead ends
Outline (topics in order, not headings):
  1. <topic> rests on <fact already in the source>
  2. ...
Not proposed: FAQ blocks for search, keyword counts, sections written for search
```

Every entity listed must already appear in the source. If the page needs a fact
the source does not hold, list it under "Missing from the source" for the owner.

### What the plan part never does

- Turns an outline topic into a heading.
- Writes a heading, a title, a description or a sentence of body copy.
- Asks for a question heading where the copy uses a claim.
- Adds a section, an FAQ or a keyword target.
- Gives a volume, a difficulty or a traffic figure without its source and date.

### Site keyword and intent map

Asked by `wugweb-strategy`. Return one table:

| Cluster | Primary phrase | Supporting phrases | Intent | Dominant page type | Existing page or new | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Then list topic gaps and pages to refresh. What to publish and when is not
this skill's decision.

### Platform keyword note

Runs only when `wugweb-work` or `wugweb-strategy` asks. Give terms for the
title, the first line and the tags on LinkedIn, Behance or Dribbble, each
sourced or marked "unvalidated". Never write the post.

### Absorbed rules

These rules were taken from the helper skills on 2026-11-16 and restated here,
so the plan part works without them. Figures marked "source's figure" are that
helper's claim, not a measured Wugweb number. The owner's rules win in any
clash.

| Rule | Source |
|---|---|
| Read intent from page one. Six or more results of one type in the top ten set the page type; otherwise mark it mixed. A page whose type differs is a type mismatch | rampstack seo-keyword, seo-skills seo-content-brief, seo-sxo |
| Two phrases share a page when their top-ten results overlap: 7 to 10 shared is one page, 4 to 6 the same cluster, 2 to 3 interlink, 0 to 1 separate (source's figures) | seo-skills seo-keyword-cluster, rampstack seo-keyword |
| Clean the phrase list first: lowercase, remove duplicates, merge singular and plural. Brand and comparison terms get their own clusters. Phrases that fit no cluster are listed apart. Each cluster names an existing page or says a new one is needed | searchfit keyword-clustering |
| Score a cluster as opportunity plus fit minus difficulty, 1 to 5 each, only where real data exists. Log deferred clusters with the reason | rampstack seo-keyword |
| Pick competitors by overlap: domains that recur in the top ten across priority phrases. A gap is a phrase where a competitor ranks in the top 20 and Wugweb does not. Note how many competitors rank; one alone may be noise. Drop competitor brand terms | rampstack seo-competitor, seo-skills seo-competitor-gap-analysis |
| The brief states what the ranking pages cover and what this page adds that they lack. The link plan lists source page, anchor and target section. Unknown volume or difficulty is written "unknown" | searchfit content-brief, seo-skills seo-content-brief |
| AI prompts usually show no search volume, so prompts are never ranked by volume | seo-skills ai-search-gaps-to-social-campaign |
| For templated page sets, such as Kits or sector pages, each page needs facts its siblings lack. Sample pages and fail the set if they differ only by name | seo-skills seo-keyword-niche, rampstack programmatic-seo |
| Platform keyword note: primary phrase early and natural, once or twice; one search intent per post; never state a volume without a tool. Tags are few and specific | social-media-skills social-seo, hashtag-strategy |
| For multi-language client sites only: research keywords per market, never translate them | searchfit content-translation |

Set aside from these helpers: heading outlines, FAQ blocks, drafted H1 and H2
lines, keyword density, volume columns with no data source.

<!-- references/audit.md -->
## Audit: checks on a rendered page

Check the page as a crawler receives it: a local preview served with the
canonical host, or the live address. The source document is not enough.

### Contents

- Scripted checks
- On-page keyphrase score
- Internal-link checks
- Absorbed rules
- Manual checks
- Crawler access
- Citability score
- Rank Math PRO net-new checks
- Fix list

### Scripted checks

`scripts/check-page.mjs` reads one HTML file. Each check has an id that appears
on every finding.

| Check id | Passes when | Severity on fail |
|---|---|---|
| `title-present` | One non-empty `<title>` | BLOCKER |
| `title-length` | Case study: source title, before " \| Wugweb", is 51 characters or fewer | BLOCKER for a case study; reported only for other types |
| `title-rendered` | Rendered title is 60 characters or fewer | HIGH |
| `description-length` | `meta name="description"` is 140 to 160 characters | HIGH |
| `h1-single` | Exactly one `<h1>` | HIGH |
| `canonical` | One absolute https canonical, on the expected host when `--host` is given | BLOCKER |
| `robots-meta` | No `noindex` | BLOCKER |
| `schema-parses` | Every JSON-LD block parses | BLOCKER |
| `schema-banned-type` | No `HowTo`, `Review` or `AggregateRating` | BLOCKER |
| `schema-faq-content` | Any `FAQPage` has at least one question in `mainEntity`. Whether each question shows on the page is a manual check | HIGH |
| `schema-required-types` | Case study: `WebPage`, `CreativeWork` and `BreadcrumbList` | HIGH |
| `schema-no-author` | Case study: `CreativeWork` has `creator` and `publisher` and no `author` | HIGH |
| `img-alt` | Every `<img>` has an `alt` attribute, empty for decoration | HIGH |
| `img-dimensions` | Every `<img>` has `width` and `height` | MEDIUM |
| `server-html-text` | At least 150 words of text in the server HTML | MEDIUM |
| `share-tags` | All 12 share tags present: `og:title`, `og:type`, `og:description`, `og:url`, `og:site_name`, `og:image`, `og:image:alt`, `twitter:card`, `twitter:title`, `twitter:description`, `twitter:image`, `twitter:image:alt` | MEDIUM |
| `share-url` | `og:url` equals the canonical | MEDIUM |
| `schema-context` | Every JSON-LD block uses `@context` exactly `https://schema.org`. House style: schema.org accepts the http form too | LOW |

The title, description and alt text lengths are house limits. Google
publishes no character limit for a title or a description and cuts titles to
the device width (Google title links page, updated 2025-12-10; snippets page,
updated 2026-04-20).

The script matches patterns in text. It does not run JavaScript or render the
page. It prints what it did not check under "Not checked".

### Manual checks

| Check | How |
|---|---|
| Firewall and bot settings | A bot setting can return 403 to crawlers while robots.txt allows them. Check the host's bot settings for every property. Cloudflare has blocked AI crawlers by default for new sign-ups since 2025-07-01. |
| Redirects | At most one hop, a house rule: Googlebot follows up to 10 (Google redirects page, updated 2026-02-04). The http, https, www and bare forms all reach one address. No redirects for old or Framer addresses. |
| Sitemap | Present, listed in robots.txt, and holding only canonical addresses that return 200. |
| Rendering | Compare the server HTML with the rendered page. Content that appears only after scripts run was invisible to the main AI crawlers in one third-party test (Vercel, 2024-12-17); no AI vendor has stated it. Google does render scripts, with a possible delay. |
| Core Web Vitals | Field data: LCP 2.5 seconds or less, INP 200 milliseconds or less, CLS 0.1 or less. |
| Schema against the page | Every value in JSON-LD is visible on the page, every `FAQPage` question included. Validate in the search engine's rich results test. Breadcrumbs have shown on desktop results only since 2025-01-23. |
| Dates | A blog post shows its date; a case study shows none. A shown date matches the schema date. |
| Images | A fault on every page using a block goes to `wugweb-kits`, which answers with its check result. |

### Crawler access

`scripts/check-robots.mjs` resolves each bot against robots.txt for one path,
using the longest matching rule.

| Group | Bots | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Search and citation | Googlebot, Bingbot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, Claude-SearchBot, Claude-User | Must be allowed on every page that should be found |
| Training | GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended, CCBot, Bytespider, meta-externalagent | The owner's choice. Report what the file says; ask once per property |

Read the table with these facts, each from the operator's own bot page as
read on 2026-11-16:

- Blocking Google-Extended does not affect Google Search. AI Overviews and AI
  Mode follow Googlebot and the snippet controls.
- A site that blocks OAI-SearchBot is not shown in ChatGPT search answers.
- ChatGPT-User and Perplexity-User fetch a page when a person asks, and may
  not follow robots.txt.

The script also flags a robots.txt with no Sitemap line, under `sitemap-listed` at HIGH.

Report, but do not require, a Content-Signal line in robots.txt (the newer
syntax some CDNs emit to signal AI usage). It is emerging and no search engine
ranks on it. Note what the file says and leave the choice to the owner.

Bot names change. Check the operator's own documentation before reporting a
bot missing.

### Citability score

Score each section of the page from 0 to 100, then weight the scores by section
length.

| Criterion | Weight | High score |
|---|---|---|
| Answer first | 30% | The first one or two sentences answer the heading |
| Self-contained | 25% | The section names its subject and reads on its own, 50 to 200 words. A GEO study puts the sweet spot at 134 to 167 words (Princeton, Georgia Tech and IIT Delhi, 2024, arXiv 2311.09735; third-party figure) |
| Structure | 20% | Clear heading order, short paragraphs, a table for any comparison of three or more |
| Specific facts | 15% | Numbers and names with their source and date |
| Original | 10% | First-party work, data or process no other page holds |

Report the page score, the three weakest sections with what each lacks, and any
site-level blocker that caps the score, such as a blocked crawler or content
that needs scripts to appear. Name what a section lacks; never write the fix.

### On-page keyphrase score

The search score, beside the citability score (the AI-answer score). Modelled on
Rank Math's client-side engine (seo-by-rank-math 1.0.280, analyzer.js). Weights
and grade bands are extracted from it, not invented. Run it with a focus
keyphrase:

```bash
node scripts/score-page.mjs <page.html> --keyword "<phrase>" [--host <host>] [--lang en] [--json]
```

One focus keyphrase per page. Each test earns fixed points; the script sums
them, normalises to the applicable maximum and returns 0 to 100. Grade bands,
the engine's own: bad 50 or less, ok 51 to 80, great over 80.

Owner decision, 2026-11-17: build the score faithful to Rank Math, no softening.
For the score only, this overrides the skill's "never propose a density target"
and "headings are claims" lines: keyword density, keyword in a subheading and
the title readability tests are scored as below. The skill still writes no copy:
it scores, `wugweb-work` acts.

Focus keyphrase:

| Test | Points | Passes when |
|---|---|---|
| keyword in title | 36 (38 non-English) | the title holds the phrase |
| keyword in permalink | 5 | the slug holds the phrase |
| keyword in the first 10% | 3 | the phrase is in the opening tenth of the body |
| keyword in content | 3 | the phrase is in the body |
| keyword in a subheading | 3 | the phrase is in an H2 to H6 |
| keyword in an image alt | 2 | the phrase is in one image's alt |
| keyword in the description | 2 | the phrase is in the meta description |
| title starts with keyword | 3 | the title begins with the phrase |
| keyword density | 0 / 2 / 3 / 6 | below 0.5% fail, 0.5 to 0.75% fair, 0.76 to 1% good, 1% or more best |
| keyword not used before | warning, 0 points | needs a site-wide phrase map; not scored yet |

Content, links, URL, title readability:

| Test | Points |
|---|---|
| content length | 2500 words or more 8, 2000 or more 5, 1500 or more 4, 1000 or more 3, 600 or more 2, else 0 |
| has image or video | images (1 is 1, 2 is 2, 3 is 4, 4 or more is 6) plus videos (1 is 1, 2 or more is 2), capped at 6 |
| short paragraphs | 3, when no paragraph runs over 120 words |
| table of contents | 2 |
| internal link present | 5 |
| external link present | 4 |
| not all links external | 2 |
| permalink length, URL 75 characters or fewer | 4 |
| title sentiment / power word / number | 1 / 1 / 1 |

Power words ship with the script as a short public list; sentiment (English
only) scores a point for any word in a small positive or negative set, null for
other languages, as Rank Math does. "Keyword not used before" stays a warning
until a site-wide phrase map exists.

### Internal-link checks

Beyond the orphan, click-depth, dead-end, generic-anchor and broken-link rules
in the absorbed set, run these on the internal links. Findings go to
`wugweb-work` (anchor wording, placement) or a developer (`rel`, redirects).
`wugweb-strategy` owns the cluster map; this skill checks the links against it.

| Check | What |
|---|---|
| anchor-text type mix | classify each internal anchor as exact, partial, branded, generic, naked or image alt; warn when exact match goes over a set share, default 20% |
| silo or cluster coherence | a cluster's supporting pages link to the hub and to each other; a link to another cluster goes to that cluster's hub, not its supporting pages |
| redirected internal links | an internal link that lands on a 301 points at the final address instead |
| internal nofollow | flag `rel=nofollow` on an internal link |
| too many links | flag a page over a set link count, default off, a house number |
| cloaked or external prefix | a path prefix the owner sets, such as `/go/`, counts as external for the mix and the audit |

### Rank Math PRO net-new checks

From the Rank Math PRO list, mapped to the Astro stack. Each is a check, not a
write.

| Check | What |
|---|---|
| VideoObject present | a page that embeds a video carries `VideoObject` with name, thumbnail, upload date and duration. Conditional: the site has little video today |
| indexed status | read Search Console URL Inspection and report indexed, excluded, or crawled and not indexed. Needs the Search Console connection |
| utility pages noindex | a thank-you, preview or download page carries `noindex` and stays out of the sitemap |
| any-URL audit | the page check reads any HTML, so it runs on a competitor's address for a side-by-side; the plan part's competitor gap uses it |

### Absorbed rules

Taken from the helper skills on 2026-11-16 and restated here, so the audit part
works without them. Figures marked "source's figure" are that helper's claim.
The owner's rules win in any clash.

| Rule | Source |
|---|---|
| Never optimise a page that is not indexable; report the indexing fault first | rampstack seo-content-audit, seo-onpage |
| Title and description are unique across the site. The title and the H1 say the same thing; the title may be shorter or carry the brand, because Google suggests putting the title text in the first `<h1>`. The description does not repeat the title | rampstack seo-onpage, brightdata seo-audit |
| Compare raw HTML with the rendered page: title, H1, description, canonical and robots must match. Never report a tag missing from a Markdown fetch; confirm in raw HTML or write "not checked" | seo-skills seo-technical-audit, seo-firecrawl |
| Key facts are text in server HTML, not held in images, PDFs or iframes. A 200 page with almost no body text is a soft 404 | rampstack seo-aeo-geo, seo-skills seo-technical-audit, aeotester audit |
| Check the `X-Robots-Tag` header as well as the meta tag. Flag a page that is noindex and canonicalised elsewhere. An unknown address returns 404 or 410, not 200. Staging hosts are noindexed | searchfit technical-seo, aeotester audit, rampstack seo-technical |
| Sitemap: report indexable pages missing from it, entries with no internal links, entries that are not 200, and lastmod identical everywhere or stale. No noindexed address in it. Canonical, sitemap and internal links agree | seo-skills seo-sitemap, rampstack seo-technical, sanity seo-aeo-best-practices |
| Internal links: every target returns 200; fragment links point at an id that exists; case and trailing slash match the route. Flag dead-end pages, pages four or more clicks from home (a house rule; Google sets no click depth), generic anchors, and hubs their spokes do not link back to. A page reachable only through the sitemap is an orphan. Fix the link itself, not with a redirect | searchfit broken-links, internal-linking, rampstack programmatic-seo |
| JSON-LD: parses; `@context` exactly `https://schema.org`; absolute addresses; ISO 8601 dates; no empty values; breadcrumb items carry position, name and item; several types share one graph; present in server HTML, because Google reads JSON-LD added by scripts but other search engines and AI crawlers may not; rechecked live after deploy | seo-skills seo-schema, searchfit schema-markup, sanity seo-aeo-best-practices |
| Share tags in server HTML: the twelve in `share-tags`. `og:url` equals the canonical | searchfit seo-audit, sanity seo-aeo-best-practices, aeotester audit |
| Images: alt present, 10 to 125 characters (a house limit; Google sets no alt length), not a file name, not repeated, not a repeated keyword; the largest image not lazy and given high fetch priority; width and height set; below-fold images lazy. Weight is reported as a fact, never fixed by re-encoding. A fault on every page using a block goes to `wugweb-kits` | seo-skills seo-images |
| Favicon, title, description and share image are present | website-design web-review |
| Slug lowercase and hyphenated; excerpt and description match the piece; decorative images take empty alt | rampstack content-and-copy, marketing content-creation |
| Citability blockers: no answer in the first 300 words; no visible date on time-sensitive content; the entity not named in full at first mention; a statistic without a primary source and data date. Visible dates match schema dates. No date change without a real edit | seo-skills seo-content-audit, rampstack seo-aeo-geo, sanity seo-aeo-best-practices |
| Cannibalisation: flag any phrase where two of the site's own pages rank or swap. Skip pages under three months old (source's figure). The owner decides which page keeps it | rampstack seo-content-audit, seo-skills seo-page |
| One verdict per page: keep, refresh, or raise with the owner. Under five ranking queries, say the data is insufficient (source's figure) | seo-skills seo-page |
| Before and after a deploy, snapshot title, description, H1, canonical, robots, lang, JSON-LD types, word count and internal links. A change to canonical, robots, lang or H1 is red; to title, description or schema is amber | seo-skills seo-drift |
| Rank each fix by the page's traffic, whether it touches indexing, crawling, rendering or vitals, and effort. Group issues with one template cause into one fix. Name the proof metric before the fix ships. Label a fix mechanical or needing the owner's facts | rampstack seo-site-health-audit, aeotester fix |
| Every finding carries its evidence. Unmeasured items are listed as out of scope with the tool that would measure them | brightdata seo-audit |
| Judge Core Web Vitals on field data at the 75th percentile, not lab runs. A declared canonical that differs from the one the search engine chose is critical | seo-skills seo-google |
| A page that already passes is a valid result | cloudflare web-perf |
| For multi-language sites only: each page lists itself, alternates link back, one x-default, tags only on the canonical address | seo-skills seo-hreflang, searchfit content-translation |

Set aside: FAQPage for questions the page does not show, HowTo, review stars, aggregate ratings, `llms.txt`,
question headings, author bylines, word-count floors, title limits of 50 to 60
and description limits of 150 to 160, redirects as a default fix, image
re-encoding.

### Fix list

```
One page (to wugweb-work, as current → proposed)
1. <section>: <what is missing>. Check: <how to confirm>

Every page using a block (to wugweb-kits)
1. <block>: <finding>, on <pages>

Code (to a developer)
1. BLOCKER <change>. Check: <how to confirm>
```

Decline and record any helper finding that asks for a banned schema type,
`llms.txt`, a keyword density, a question heading in place of a claim, or a
rewrite of approved copy.

## Report: search and AI answer performance

The report part reads data and says what to improve next. It is advisory. It
changes nothing.

### Name the source of every number

| Need | Without a connected tool | With a connected tool |
|---|---|---|
| Clicks, impressions, click rate, position | A Search Console export | The Search Console API, or an SEO data tool |
| Phrase volume and difficulty | Search Console queries | An SEO data tool, with its date |
| Speed | PageSpeed Insights | The same, by script |
| AI answer presence | A fixed prompt sample run by hand | An AI visibility tool |

A Search Console export is the standard source, set by the owner. A connected
tool is optional. If no export is given, ask for it and stop.

### The monthly report

```
Site: <host> | Period: <dates> | Source: <tool, date fetched>

Totals: clicks, impressions, click rate, average position
  against the previous period: <change>
  against the same period last year: <change>

Rose most: <page>, <change>, ...
Fell most: <page>, <change>, ...

Quick wins
  Title and description: <queries with many impressions and a low click rate>
  Content: <pages at positions 8 to 20>

AI answers: <n> prompts; cited <n>, mentioned <n>, absent <n>; trend over <months>

Not checked: <anything the data did not cover>
```

Search Console data is sampled and leaves some queries out. Read it as a trend.

Facts about the data, from Google's and Bing's own pages as read on 2026-11-16:

- Clicks and impressions from AI Overviews and AI Mode are counted inside the
  Web totals. Say so beside the totals.
- Search Console's Generative AI performance report, live for all sites since
  2026-08-31, shows impressions.
- The Search Console table in the browser stops at 1,000 rows. Use the export
  or the API for more.
- Bing Webmaster Tools has an AI Performance report, in preview since
  2026-02-10, that shows citations in its AI answers.

### AI answer sample

1. Fix a list of prompts a buyer would ask, in the owner's words. Keep it the
   same each month.
2. Run each prompt several times in the AI tools that matter to the owner. The
   same prompt gives different answers each run, so one run is not evidence.
   Report how often Wugweb appears across the runs, not a single result.
3. Log each result as cited (a Wugweb page is linked), mentioned (Wugweb is
   named) or absent.
4. Read the trend over several months. A single month moves a lot.

### Diagnose a drop

Check in this order and stop at the first cause found:

1. Tracking: did the measurement itself break?
2. Indexing: did robots.txt, a noindex, a canonical or a deploy change?
3. Search engine update: does the drop line up with a published update date?
4. Results features: did an AI answer or another feature take the click?
5. Competitors: did another page take the position?
6. Content decay: is the page out of date?

### Limits on use

- Never place these numbers on a case study as a client result.
- Never estimate a missing number. Say it is missing.

### Absorbed rules

Taken from the helper skills on 2026-11-16 and restated here, so the report
part works without them. The owner's rules win in any clash.

| Rule | Source |
|---|---|
| Before any diagnosis, confirm the drop is real: Search Console clicks and analytics sessions move together. Restate the question with the metric, dates and figures | rampstack seo-traffic-diagnosis, analytics analytics-diagnostic-method |
| Read the shape first. A one-step cliff points to a deploy, tracking or an outage; a slow ramp to decay; a one-day spike to a bot or a viral moment. Every channel falling together points to measurement. Compare the same weekdays | analytics traffic-change-diagnosis |
| Split by country, device, section, and branded or not. Position steady with click rate down means a results feature took the click. If the total moved and no segment did, it is a mix change. End with one evidenced hypothesis; if two causes fit, report both and say what data would separate them | rampstack seo-traffic-diagnosis, analytics skills |
| Search Console data lags two to three days. State the sample size first. Call a trend only with enough points. A benchmark is never a target | seo-skills seo-google, analytics metric-context-and-benchmarks, marketing performance-report |
| Junk-traffic check for organic: pages per session near one, very short visits, very low engagement, off-market geography, spam referrers. Direct traffic absorbs branded search | analytics channel-and-funnel-quality |
| AI answer sample: fixed prompt types (best in category, brand against rival, alternatives, a how-to for the problem, a recommendation for a use case). Per engine, record named, linked as a source, or absent, plus position, whether the description is accurate, and which competitors were named. Use fresh sessions. Zero stays zero. Citation rate is cited over answers present | searchfit ai-visibility, seo-skills seo-ai-search-share-of-voice, seo-geo, `social-media-skills:ai-search-optimization` |
| Report visits referred by AI assistants as their own line. ChatGPT links carry `utm_source=chatgpt.com` (third-party claim: SearchPilot, 2026-05-13); some AI apps pass no referrer, so the line undercounts | sanity seo-aeo-best-practices, `social-media-skills:ai-search-optimization` |
| Lead with outcomes, include what underperformed, and close with three ranked actions. Each action cites its data point, impact and effort | social-media-skills analytics-and-reporting, marketing performance-report |

Set aside: recovery forecasts as numbers, generic benchmark ranges, redirects
from old paths as a fix, scores with no rubric.
